package.title: 100 NAT-IE-Style Chemistry MCQs on Atomic Structure and Bonding

questions.question: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of which particles in its nucleus?
An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
Two atoms of the same element have different numbers of neutrons. They are called:
How many electrons are in a neutral sodium atom with atomic number 11?
A particle has 3 protons and 4 neutrons. What is its mass number?
According to the 2n-squared rule, what is the maximum electron capacity of the third shell?
How many orbitals are present in a p subshell?
What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy one orbital?
What is the azimuthal quantum number l for an s subshell?
Which subshell is filled immediately after 2s in the usual Aufbau filling order?
The Aufbau principle says that electrons in a ground-state atom generally occupy:
choices: Orbitals in order of their shapes

questions.question: According to the Pauli exclusion principle, two electrons in the same orbital must have:
Hund's rule predicts that electrons fill equal-energy orbitals by:
choices: Pairing in one orbital before occupying others
Occupying separate orbitals with parallel spins first
Taking opposite spins in every orbital

questions.question: What is the ground-state electron configuration of magnesium, atomic number 12?
Which subshell is the last occupied in the ground-state electron configuration of chlorine, atomic number 17?
Which is the ground-state configuration of iron, atomic number 26, using noble-gas shorthand?
Which ground-state configuration represents chromium, atomic number 24?
Which ground-state configuration represents copper, atomic number 29?
How many electrons are in the outermost shell of a neutral sodium atom?
A positive ion is formed from a neutral atom when the atom:
How many electrons are in an O2- ion? Oxygen has atomic number 8.
How many electrons are in a Cl- ion? Chlorine has atomic number 17.
An element has isotopes of mass 10 u at 20% abundance and mass 11 u at 80% abundance. What is its average atomic mass?
For electromagnetic radiation, what happens to photon energy when frequency increases?
If the frequency of light increases, its wavelength in a vacuum:
For a main-group element, the period number generally indicates the number of:
Elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are commonly called:
Which group contains the noble gases in the modern periodic table?
Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally:
Moving down a group, atomic radius generally:
For main-group elements across a period, electronegativity generally:
Which element has the greatest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
For elements within a group, metallic character generally increases:
choices: From left to right across a period

questions.question: For main-group elements across a period, first ionization energy generally tends to:
Which atom has the lower first ionization energy: potassium or sodium?
Which species has the largest radius among O2-, F- and Na+?
Which third-period atom is generally the largest in atomic radius?
A main-group atom has the electron arrangement 2,8,7. Which group does it belong to?
A main-group atom has the electron arrangement 2,8,2. Which group does it belong to?
Which oxide is generally basic when dissolved or reacted with acid?
Which oxide is an acidic oxide that forms an acid when it reacts with water?
Electron affinity is concerned with the energy change when a gaseous atom:
Why does shielding generally increase down a group?
choices: More inner electron shells are present
The nucleus loses all its protons

questions.question: In a typical ionic bond between a metal and a non-metal, the bond forms primarily through:
choices: Transfer of electrons followed by electrostatic attraction

questions.question: What is the principal bonding arrangement in solid sodium chloride?
choices: A lattice of Na+ and Cl- ions
Separate NaCl molecules linked by hydrogen bonds
A network of neutral sodium atoms
A lattice of shared electron pairs between Na and Cl

questions.question: What is the simplest formula for a compound made from Mg2+ and Cl- ions?
What is the simplest formula for a neutral compound made from Al3+ and O2- ions?
A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
choices: Share one or more pairs of electrons

questions.question: How many shared electron pairs are present in a single covalent bond?
How many shared electron pairs are present in a double covalent bond?
How many shared electron pairs are present in a triple covalent bond?
A coordinate covalent bond forms when the shared electron pair is:
choices: Supplied equally as one electron from each atom in all cases
Transferred completely to form only a neutral atom

questions.question: In a Lewis electron-dot symbol, the dots around an element symbol usually represent its:
How many electrons are needed in the first shell for hydrogen to reach a filled shell?
Why do many ionic solids have high melting points?
choices: Strong electrostatic attractions hold their ions in a lattice
Their ions are free to move in the solid
Their molecules are held together only by weak dispersion forces

questions.question: Why can molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?
choices: Its ions are mobile and carry charge
Its electrons are all removed from the atoms
Its ions are fixed in place

questions.question: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity well?
choices: Its ions are held in fixed lattice positions
All its electrons move freely through the solid

questions.question: Why does aqueous sodium chloride solution conduct electricity?
choices: Dissolved Na+ and Cl- ions can move through the solution
Water molecules turn into metal atoms
The solution contains no charged species

questions.question: Which description best fits a typical small covalent molecular substance such as methane?
choices: It is necessarily a giant ionic lattice
It contains only free metal ions
It always conducts electricity as a solid

questions.question: The formula NaCl represents the simplest ratio of ions in the solid. This ratio is called a:
Which bond is expected to be polar because the atoms have different electronegativities?
Which bond is nonpolar because it joins identical atoms?
A bond dipole points, by the usual chemistry convention, toward the atom that is:
What is the formal charge on nitrogen in the ammonium ion, NH4+?
In the common Lewis structure of carbon dioxide, the carbon atom is joined to each oxygen by a:
How many lone pairs are on the nitrogen atom in a typical Lewis structure of NH3?
How many lone pairs are on the oxygen atom in a typical Lewis structure of H2O?
What is the molecular shape of CH4?
What is the molecular shape of CO2?
What is the molecular shape of BF3?
What is the molecular shape of NH3?
What is the molecular shape of H2O?
The approximate H-C-H bond angle in tetrahedral methane is:
The carbon atoms in ethene, C2H4, each have which local geometry?
The carbon atoms in ethyne, C2H2, each have which local geometry?
Which hybridization is commonly assigned to the carbon atom in methane?
Which hybridization is commonly assigned to the carbon atom in CO2?
Which hybridization is commonly assigned to boron in BF3?
Which hybridization is commonly assigned to nitrogen in NH3 in the basic valence-bond model?
A sigma bond is formed by orbitals overlapping:
choices: Sideways above and below the internuclear axis only

questions.question: A pi bond is formed primarily by:
choices: Head-on overlap along the internuclear axis

questions.question: How many sigma bonds are present in a single covalent bond?
A double covalent bond consists of:
choices: One sigma bond and one pi bond
One sigma bond and two pi bonds

questions.question: A triple covalent bond consists of:
choices: Two sigma bonds and one pi bond
One sigma bond and two pi bonds

questions.question: What is the bond order of the nitrogen-nitrogen bond in N2?
Which statement about H-Cl is correct?
choices: It has a polar covalent bond
It has a nonpolar covalent bond
It has an ionic bond between identical ions

questions.question: Which substance can form hydrogen bonds between its molecules in the pure liquid?
Why does water have a higher boiling point than a similar-sized molecule with only weak dispersion forces?
choices: Water molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds
Water molecules are ionic solids at room temperature
Water has a greater number of protons per molecule

questions.question: London dispersion forces arise from:
Which intermolecular attraction is especially important between nonpolar I2 molecules?
Which attraction is characteristic between neighbouring polar HCl molecules?
choices: Hydrogen bonding between H and Cl

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares hydrogen bonding with covalent bonding in water?
choices: Hydrogen bonds are attractions between molecules; O-H covalent bonds are within a molecule
They are two names for the same bond
O-H covalent bonds occur only between separate water molecules
Hydrogen bonds join oxygen nuclei into one nucleus

questions.question: Which pair of ions has the same number of electrons?
What is the simplest formula for a neutral compound made from Ca2+ and PO4 3- ions?
How many total valence electrons are in the ammonium ion, NH4+?
Which Lewis description of the carbonate ion, CO3 2-, is correct?
choices: It has three identical C-O bonds in each resonance hybrid
It has one permanent C=O bond and two permanently different C-O bonds
It has a linear arrangement around carbon

questions.question: Which statement best describes BF3 with respect to the octet rule?
choices: Boron has an incomplete octet in its usual Lewis structure
Boron has ten electrons around it
Each fluorine has an incomplete duet
The molecule has no covalent bonds

questions.question: Which molecule is commonly described as having an expanded octet around its central atom?
When NH3 accepts H+ to form NH4+, the nitrogen atom acts as a:
Which is expected to have stronger ionic attractions in its solid lattice, MgO or NaCl, based on ionic charges alone and comparable separation?
